summary: The proactive pass is handed who is in the room and what they are called there, instead of searching memory for every nickname a note is written in.
details: A note's body is written in whatever the group calls each other, and the roster holds the mapped name; nothing joined the two. The design's own rule — inject the index, call for depth — had been implemented for notes and for rooms and for nothing else, so every unknown handle cost a tool call. One live pass spent six of ten calls on the same search asking who these people were, until a guard stopped it.
The index is read through the same room the tag path uses, so a pass and a turn cannot hold two ideas of who is in a room. A platform with no roster renders no block.

The suite grading this could not have caught it: its room held one synthetic person with no aliases, so the failure was not expressible. It now holds four people with the handles the group actually types.

And the grader can now bound what a decision COST, not only whether it was right. It graded what was written and never how many memory reads it took to get there — which is the whole shape of this defect.
limitations: The index does not stop the over-reading on its own: with it in front of her she still spends three to five memory reads on a decision the prompt already answers. That case now fails on purpose, and is the measurement for whatever fixes it.
The suite still fails on the older case where she schedules a nudge for the day of an event rather than the day before.
